episode_summary: Season 2 episode 8 of The Bitcoin Podcast (Nov 2025), recorded with two hosts (Corey absent). Mostly banter, but the hosts riff on Coinbase's Web3 wallet and Base chain, airdrop claims, Tether's profits, real-world asset tokenization (houses, stocks, BlackRock funds, ERC-1155 vs per-asset contracts), Zcash price action and privacy-coin pump cycles, and EV stocks. Few hard numbers; many opinions and loose predictions.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said Tether had made $10 billion in the first nine months of that year, which he found hard to square with a stablecoin.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Tether made $10 billion in the first nine months of this year. And I'm like, how does a stable coin make $10 billion?

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host argued that Bitcoin adoption was nearing its peak and that the asset was becoming a commoditised stock, endorsed by the White House and many governments.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: So I think we're, we're nearing the peak of what actual Bitcoin adoption looks like.

cards.claim: In November 2025 the hosts disagreed over whether Bitcoin's benefits were being delivered through price action, with one saying it was very institutionalised.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: I think it's very institutionalized. I mean, the benefit that you're speaking as price action, right?

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said Bitcoin was no closer to the reliable financial system it promised, because the market was fragmenting into many stablecoins.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I don't think we're close to that anymore, right? Everything's fragmenting. It's a bunch of stable coins.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said Coinbase had gone full circle from refusing crypto features to launching a Web3 wallet and the Base chain, while claiming alignment with Ethereum.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: they did the wallet and they're like uh yeah we're really aligned with ethereum we want to make sure that their roadmap comes to completion

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host accused Coinbase of hoarding users' money from forks and airdrops that users had never claimed.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: coinbase is hoarding a lot of people's money and they're just hoping everyone forgets about it

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host pointed listeners to Lofty as a platform that pays token holders a percentage of rent on tokenised property.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Go to Lofty. It pays you a percentage of the rent.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said attempts to tokenise fractional real estate equity had been tried often but never scaled, and that he had not seen a working platform.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: we haven't we've seen this attempted a lot never scales so i don't know

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host argued privacy tokens get pumped late in the crypto cycle because they are an easy narrative on a small market cap.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i think it's because it's an easy kind of narrative to pump it's an easy thing to kind of work with and on top of that it's a such a smaller market cap

cards.claim: In November 2025 the hosts joked that crypto runs a three-pump cycle, with Bitcoin pumping first, then altcoins, and privacy coins last.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Crypto is the three pump chump market. You got a Bitcoin pumps, then alt's pump, and then privacy coins pump.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said Zcash's price had surged because traders moved funds through shielded transactions, which pushed up demand for a limited ZEC supply.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Zcash is like blown up like price wise because, you know, when people do a bunch of trades and they don't want to let people know what they're going to do with the money.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said privacy is largely fake, since anyone who really wants to find someone will be able to.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: privacy to me gets interesting but also not interesting because i know it's like fake so it's just like you know privacy is fake

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host argued that in this day and age anyone who wants to find you will find you, so privacy is a weak promise.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: if somebody wants to find you, you'll be found.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said the DevConnect developer event was next month in Argentina, running from November 17 to 21.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: yeah you gotta go to dev you gotta go to dev connect that's uh next month in argentina

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host named Custodia as an example of a crypto bank being set up by wealthy players.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i think it's called custodia okay custodia is one of them where it's like interesting

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said people would not self-custody their own crypto, and that they had wrongly expected everyone to use a hardware wallet ten years earlier.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: people aren't going to custody their own crypto like people don't want that smoke.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said stocks and securities were the easiest real-world assets to tokenise, since a blockchain could expose them to buyers worldwide.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I think the easiest real world asset to see tokenizing is stocks and securities.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said he had considered buying Kia stock two years earlier on the view that electric vehicles would take off in the US, but dropped the idea because of foreign-stock rules.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i thought electric vehicles were going to take off here in the States. So I was like, oh, let me be a smart guy.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said BlackRock was planning to tokenise one of its funds so buyers could hold tokens representing partial ownership.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: literally BlackRock is like, hey, we're going to tokenize our fund and you can buy tokens of our fund that represent a partial ownership of the

cards.claim: In November 2025 the hosts summarised that tokenised assets can use one contract per asset, which gives clear legal ownership but does not scale, or one shared ERC-1155 contract, which is cheaper but less legally isolated.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It doesn't scale. Or one shared contract for many assets like an ERC-1155.

cards.claim: In November 2025 a host said electric vehicles would still take off in the US, though not as dramatically as he had expected, citing a Cadillac with a 500-mile range.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i'm just like dude electrics cars are going to take off here in the states now do i think they're taking off as vertical as I thought they would? No.

title: The Bitcoin Podcast S02E08 - Hacks, ZCash, and Air Fryers
